title: Presheaf Čech vanishing implies derived cohomology vanishing
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a Grothendieck site and $F$ an abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Suppose that for every map $f:P\to Q$ of presheaves of sets whose values lie in the universe of $F$, the complex $\check C^\bullet(f,F)$ [def-sc-presheaf-cech-complex] has zero cohomology in each positive degree. Then $H^q(U,F)=0$ for every $U\in\mathcal C$ and $q>0$, where $H^q(U,F)$ is Mathlib Sheaf.H', equivalently Ext from the sheafified free abelian representable. HasSheafify and HasExt are assumed as in that definition. The site need not have pullbacks and its object and morphism universes need not agree.

source.place: Tags 03F9 and 079Z; presheaf-nerve vanishing variant using Yoneda extensions and the first-quadrant descent spectral sequence

proof.text: Write Z[P] for the sheafified free abelian presheaf on P. Induct on q>0 simultaneously for all small-valued P. Represent an Ext class from Z[P] to F by a finite Yoneda extension, ending in an epimorphism G → Z[P]. The presheaf E of lifts of the generator map P → Z[P] is small-valued and E → P is locally surjective. The class pulls back to zero on Z[E] because the last epimorphism splits after this pullback.

source.place: Tag 03F9 induction principle; generalized sections in Section 079V; finite Yoneda Ext and local lifting

proof.text: The augmented sheafified free nerve of E → P is exact, by fibrewise free nerve resolution and exact sheafification. Its derived Hom filtration gives the spectral sequence of Tag 079Z, E_1^(a,b)=Ext^b(Z[E_a],F) ⇒ Ext^(a+b)(Z[P],F). In a fixed degree only a finite first-quadrant range matters. This is also a Yoneda-Ext spectral sequence and does not require an extra enough-injectives hypothesis in the theorem signature.

Induction kills rows 0<b<q, and the hypothesis kills positive cohomology of the zero row, which is exactly presheafCechComplex(E → P,F). The other filtration pieces in total degree q are therefore zero, so the edge map to Ext^q(Z[E],F) is injective. The class has zero image and is zero. For q=1 there are no intermediate rows. Take P=yoneda(U) to obtain H'(F,q,U).
